lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Stop-Frame Animation Studio
lesson.summary: Plan a storyboard, take frames with tiny moves, keep the shots steady and review and share an animation fairly.
learning_objectives: Explain how frames and frame rate make still pictures seem to move
Plan an animation with a storyboard and small moves
Keep frames consistent, then review, credit and share

standards.text: Select, use and combine a variety of software on digital devices to design and create digital content, including animation
Evaluate digital content and use technology respectfully, crediting the work of others

success_criteria: I can say what a frame and frame rate are
I can plan with a storyboard and work out frames needed
I can keep shots steady and review my animation
lesson.real_life: Making a short clay animation for Eid or Hunza, then sharing it with credits at a school film festival.

warm_up.explanation: A pixel is one tiny square.

options.text: One tiny square of a picture

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do still pictures seem to move?
blocks.say: Today we make a model move. How can still pictures look like real movement?

blocks.alt: Four black picture frames on a white wall, each holding a similar small photo of a coast, with tiny differences
blocks.caption: Four almost-identical pictures. Animation is a long series like this, played very fast.
blocks.credit: Photo by Andrea De Santis on Unsplash
blocks.say: Zara and Hamza want to animate a clay apricot rolling across a table. Look at these four pictures. They are almost the same.

blocks.markdown: A **frame** is one single picture in an animation.
blocks.say: In stop-frame animation, we take a photo, move the model a tiny bit, and take another photo. Each photo is a frame.

blocks.markdown: Played fast, many still frames seem to move.
blocks.say: When we play the frames fast, our brain joins them up. The model seems to move by itself.

scenes.caption: Frame 1.
scenes.say: Frame one: the clay apricot sits at the left of the table.

scenes.caption: Frames 2 and 3.
scenes.say: Frame two: the apricot is a tiny bit further right. Frame three: a little further.

scenes.caption: Playing.
scenes.say: Played quickly, the apricot appears to roll across the table.

question.prompt: An animation has 24 photos. What is each photo called?
question.explanation: Each picture in an animation is a frame.

blocks.markdown: **Frame rate** is how many frames are shown each second.
blocks.say: Frame rate is the number of frames shown each second. Many stop-frame films use about twelve frames a second.

scenes.caption: One second.
scenes.say: At twelve frames a second, one second of film needs twelve photos.

scenes.caption: Five seconds.
scenes.say: Five seconds needs sixty photos. That is a lot of tiny moves.

scenes.caption: Patience.
scenes.say: So animators plan carefully and work patiently.

question.prompt: Played quickly, a series of still pictures can seem to move.
question.explanation: Quick playback of many frames gives the idea of movement.

blocks.title: Zara's rolling apricot
blocks.transcript: Zara and Hamza want to animate a clay apricot. They draw a storyboard first. The camera sits on a tripod. The lamp stays in one place. Photo, tiny move, photo. Every photo is a frame. At twelve frames a second, five seconds needs sixty frames. They play it fast. The apricot seems to roll by itself. At frame forty, the picture jumps. The camera was bumped. They retake the frames. Now it is smooth. They add sound, credit the music, and share it with the class.
blocks.caption: Zara and Hamza animate a clay apricot and fix a jump.

points: A frame is one picture in an animation
Played fast, many frames seem to move
Frame rate is the number of frames each second
blocks.say: Let us remember. Frames are photos with tiny changes. Played fast, they seem to move.

blocks.markdown: A **storyboard** is a set of drawn boxes that plans each scene.
blocks.say: Zara and Hamza plan before they take any photos. They draw a storyboard.

scenes.caption: Beginning.
scenes.say: Box one: the apricot sits at the edge of the table. This is the beginning.

scenes.caption: Middle.
scenes.say: Box two: it rolls across the table and bumps a book. This is the middle.

scenes.caption: End.
scenes.say: Box three: the apricot stops, and a happy clay bird lands on it. This is the end.

blocks.title: Sort the planning jobs
blocks.goal: Move the 6 jobs into Before filming or While filming.

question.prompt: Zara draws six boxes that show what happens in each scene. What is she making?
question.explanation: A set of drawn scene boxes is a storyboard.

blocks.markdown: Tiny moves look smooth. Big jumps look jerky.
blocks.say: To make the apricot roll smoothly, they move it a tiny bit between photos. Big jumps look jerky.

blocks.markdown: Plan how many frames you need.
blocks.say: They count how many frames they need. Ten seconds at twelve frames a second is a hundred and twenty photos.

scenes.caption: Tiny.
scenes.say: A tiny move each time: the apricot glides smoothly across the table.

scenes.caption: Big.
scenes.say: A big jump each time: the apricot seems to teleport and looks jerky.

blocks.title: Plan an animation
instructions: Draw a storyboard with three boxes: beginning, middle and end.
Decide how many seconds each box will last.
Work out how many frames you need at twelve frames a second.
blocks.say: Now you try. Plan a short animation with a partner.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Plan with a storyboard. Move the model in tiny steps.

blocks.markdown: **Consistent** frames match each other in light, background and camera position.
blocks.say: When the apricot rolls, the table, light and camera must stay the same. That is called being consistent.

blocks.alt: A box of bright modelling clay sticks in black, purple, blue, green, red, orange, white and yellow on a wooden table
blocks.caption: Modelling clay is easy to shape and move in tiny steps.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ksenia Pixelesse on Unsplash
blocks.say: Zara and Hamza make their characters from modelling clay. Clay is easy to move in small steps.

scenes.caption: Camera.
scenes.say: The camera sits on a tripod. If it moves, the whole picture jumps.

scenes.caption: Light.
scenes.say: The lamp stays on the same spot. Changing light makes the frames flicker.

scenes.caption: Hands out.
scenes.say: Hands stay out of the picture. Only the model moves.

question.prompt: The camera is knocked sideways between two photos. What happens?
question.explanation: A moved camera makes the frames jump.

blocks.markdown: **Onion skin** shows a faint copy of the last frame.
blocks.say: Many programs have an onion skin. It shows a faint copy of the last frame over the live view.

blocks.markdown: Use onion skin to place the next move. Play the memory game.
blocks.say: It helps Zara line up the next tiny move. First a memory game.

blocks.markdown: To **review** is to look carefully and decide what to improve.
blocks.say: Zara and Hamza finish taking photos. Now they play the animation back all the way through.

blocks.markdown: Find the problem. Retake the frames.
blocks.say: They spot a jump in frame forty. They retake those frames with the camera steady.

blocks.markdown: Add sound, then play it again.
blocks.say: They add a sound of rolling and a little bird song. Then they play it again.

scenes.caption: Playback.
scenes.say: They play it back. The apricot jumps at frame forty.

scenes.caption: Fix.
scenes.say: The camera had been bumped. They fix the tripod and retake the frames.

scenes.caption: Better.
scenes.say: Now it is smooth. They add sound and enjoy their work.

question.prompt: Put the steps of reviewing an animation in order.
question.explanation: Watch, note, fix, then add sound.

items.text: Note what is jerky or unclear
Play it all the way through

blocks.say: Good feedback says one thing that worked and one idea to improve. It is kind and clear.

blocks.markdown: Ask permission and give credit before sharing.
blocks.say: Before sharing, they ask permission if people appear. They credit any music they borrow.

scenes.caption: Feedback.
scenes.say: Another group watches. They say: your apricot rolls smoothly. Try a longer ending.

scenes.caption: Improve.
scenes.say: Zara and Hamza note the idea and decide to add a longer ending.

scenes.caption: Share.
scenes.say: They credit the free music and share the film with their class.

blocks.title: Review plan
instructions: Write one thing you want to check, such as smooth moves.
Watch a partner's animation. Write one good thing and one idea.
Say how you will credit any music or pictures you use.
blocks.say: Now you try. Plan how you will review your animation.
